samuel2.4.p1.b1.text: Now when Ish-bosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost courage, and all Israel was dismayed.

samuel2.4.p1.b2.text: Saul’s son had two men who were leaders of raiding parties. One was named Baanah and the other Rechab; they were sons of Rimmon the Beerothite of the tribe of Benjamin

samuel2.4.p2.b1.text: And Jonathan son of Saul had a son who was lame in his feet. … His name was Mephibosheth.

samuel2.4.p2.b2.text: His nurse picked him up and fled, but as she was hurrying to escape, he fell and became lame.

samuel2.4.p2.b3.text: Rechab and Baanah … arrived at the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while the king was taking his midday nap.

samuel2.4.p2.b4.text: They entered the interior of the house as if to get some wheat, …

samuel2.4.p3.b1.text: … took his head, and traveled all night by way of the Arabah. They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron …

samuel2.4.p3.b2.text: Here is the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy who sought your life. Today the LORD has granted vengeance to my lord the king against Saul and his offspring.

samuel2.4.p4.b1.text: As surely as the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from all distress, …

samuel2.4.p4.b2.text: when someone told me, ‘Look, Saul is dead,’ and thought he was a bearer of good news, I seized him and put him to death at Ziklag. …

samuel2.4.p4.b3.text: How much more, when wicked men kill a righteous man in his own house and on his own bed, shall I not now require his blood from your hands and remove you from the earth!”

samuel2.4.p4.b4.text: but they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in Abner’s tomb in Hebron.
